transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-04-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ravi Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (AtlasPay CTO), Maya Patel (AtlasPay SRE), Sam Rogers (AtlasPay PM)

Summary: Weekly POC sync for pilot rollout and go-live planning. Focus on canary strategy, cutover checklist, monitoring dashboards, runbooks, and outstanding blockers (staging access, benchmarks).

00:00 Jordan Lee: okay um hi everyone, thanks for joining, we have about 45 minutes i think, uh we'll start with current state, then canary then monitoring then next steps
00:12 Alex Martinez: great thanks Jordan, hey team, quick agenda bump - confirm cutover window, canary slices, rollback gates and who owns runbooks, also we'll talk about monitoring instrumentation and alerts
00:28 Maya Patel: sounds good. we still need staging VPC access for Redwood to run a few end-to-end tests, i put a ticket in but it's not done yet
00:40 Priya Nair: got it, maya. we can run synthetic traffic once we have VPC peering, and we'll also push the quantized variant to staging for latency/cost numbers
00:55 Jordan Lee: how long do you think that benchmark will take? we want p95 latency under 300ms for interactive flows
01:05 Priya Nair: ballpark 1-2 hours of runs to collect stable p95 across loads; if we do warm KV caching it might show better tail latency. note: our quantized model has slightly different memory/KV behavior so we'll measure both
01:22 Ravi Shah: also worth noting that on Dedicated we saw consistent throughput, but in hosted mode the burst policy matters, just throwing that out since AtlasPay is evaluating dedicated vs hosted for the pilot
01:35 Sam Rogers: right, our preference is dedicated for production but pilot can be hosted if the SLA is acceptable. cost is also a factor
01:48 Alex Martinez: understood. for the canary we recommend a progressive ramp: day 1 1% traffic for 6 hours, day 2 5% for 12 hours, day 3 25% for 24 hours then ramp to full if gates pass. canary gates are error rate < 0.5% and p95 within 10% of baseline
02:10 Jordan Lee: baseline meaning current service before Redwood? or baseline from staging?
02:16 Alex Martinez: baseline as measured in your control path - ideally pre-Redwood average p95. we can also compute relative regression against staging during bench runs
02:30 Maya Patel: what about A/B vs canary? we want some A/B signal for quality - check if model responses skew on a few intents
02:39 Priya Nair: yeah we can run both - traffic slice can be routed with feature flags so A/B sampling can capture quality metrics. we'll set up automatic sampling of 10% of canary traffic for human eval and metrics around relevancy
02:58 Jordan Lee: human eval is expensive though, do we have automated heuristics?
03:05 Priya Nair: we can track confidence scores, token-level changes, rerank deltas, and user engagement proxies. plus logs for manual review if thresholds cross
03:20 Sam Rogers: for rollback criteria, what are the exact thresholds? latency, error rate, and quality drop?
03:28 Alex Martinez: propose: immediate rollback if error rate > 1% for 15 minutes, or p95 increases > 20% sustained for 30 minutes. quality drop: if automated relevancy metric drops > 10% over baseline or human eval fails a sample, then pause and investigate
03:49 Jordan Lee: that seems reasonable. will that integrate with our incident management? we use PagerDuty
03:55 Maya Patel: yes, we need alerts wired into pagerduty and slack. also SSO test accounts for Redwood to access the console
04:08 Alex Martinez: we'll provide the alert templates and the runbook steps; Priya will share the dashboard definitions to import into your Grafana or Redwood Console
04:20 Ravi Shah: small heads up - sometimes transcriptions and SLO names differ between systems; we'll codify metric IDs in the runbook to avoid confusion
04:31 Maya Patel: good, please include exact metric names and tags (env: staging/prod, cluster, route)
04:38 Priya Nair: will do. also we'll include cost per 1k tokens metric for canary so you can judge economics as traffic ramps
04:48 Jordan Lee: regarding cutover checklist
04:52 Alex Martinez: typical cutover items: freeze model changes day before, validate staging smoke tests, schedule DB/feature-flag toggles, notify support and on-call, ensure A/B logging enabled, enable canary routing, and ensure rollback playbook is live
05:10 Sam Rogers: do we need a maintenance window? we prefer a low-traffic overnight window but that may impact onboarding teams in APAC
05:18 Jordan Lee: target is 02:00 UTC, but we'll validate with business owners; can push to 04:00 if needed
05:24 Maya Patel: also need KMS/HSM key rotation plan for encryption in transit at rest, and SAML SSO tests before cutover
05:34 Alex Martinez: Redwood supports KMS integration; we'll include key rotation steps in the runbook and SAML test items. security gating: SOC2 evidence and audit logs will be shared prior to prod cutover
05:50 Jordan Lee: perfect. any open compliance blockers?
05:54 Priya Nair: we ran through SOC2 docs last week; your security team raised a minor log-retention question which we updated in the policy doc and re-shared, but nothing blocking for pilot
06:06 Jordan Lee: good. Maya, how's the staging VPC timeline?
06:10 Maya Patel: I'm chasing infra, hoping to have peering and a test account by tomorrow morning, but network requires a ticket and an approval since it's a new CIDR range
06:20 Alex Martinez: if staging is delayed we can do an initial benchmark in Redwood-hosted staging and mask endpoints, but it's preferable to run in your VPC for realistic latency and IAM constraints
06:35 Priya Nair: agree - VPC gives realistic egress and KMS access. but we can still run smoke tests in hosted to validate logic paths
06:46 Jordan Lee: let's assume staging VPC will be ready by 2025-04-24 as Maya said. Priya, you'll run the quantized vs float benchmark there?
06:55 Priya Nair: yes, we'll run three load profiles: low (5 qps), medium (50 qps), and burst (200 qps) for 30-60 minutes each to capture p50/p95/p99 and CPU/GPU utilization and cost numbers
07:12 Sam Rogers: you'll capture KV cache warmup effects? a lot of our traffic is conversational so cache hit matters
07:20 Priya Nair: yes, we'll include cold and warm starts and show the delta; caching policy will be documented too
07:30 Jordan Lee: what about model pinning and rollbacks on the Dedicated environment - how quick is the fallback?
07:36 Ravi Shah: on Dedicated we maintain pinned model versions and a fast redeploy path; fallback can be automated to a previous snapshot within minutes, but data plane warmup may take longer so we usually recommend a short grace period
07:50 Maya Patel: can you quantify 'minutes'? if we switch back to previous model, how long until p95 stabilizes?
07:57 Ravi Shah: typically 2-6 minutes for container redeploy and 10-20 minutes to reach steady KV cache performance depending on traffic shape
08:08 Jordan Lee: ok that's acceptable. Sam, who on support will be on-call for the first 48 hours?
08:12 Sam Rogers: I'll coordinate; likely the backend on-call plus one product owner; we'll share a rota by Friday
08:20 Alex Martinez: for A/B quality checks, we'll wire a light-touch human review workflow: sample 100 responses per day from canary and flag borderline cases. Redwood can host the review UI or send CSVs to your PMs
08:34 Sam Rogers: prefer Redwood-hosted review UI for speed, but we need SSO working
08:38 Priya Nair: we'll include SSO test instructions in the onboarding checklist. also note that transcription sometimes garbles product names like KV cache etc in exports, so use metric IDs for alerts
08:52 Jordan Lee: noted. any concerns about rate limits during ramp?
08:57 Alex Martinez: we'll set per-route quotas for canary slices, and you can temporarily increase burst capacity if needed; Redwood Dedicated offers reserved throughput if you decide to commit to Dedicated for prod
09:12 Maya Patel: what's the cost delta between hosted pilot and dedicated baseline? rough estimate per 100k tokens?
09:18 Alex Martinez: ballpark: hosted pilot x cents per 1k tokens, Dedicated reduces per-token cost when you commit to reserved capacity; Priya will send an updated spreadsheet with run numbers post-benchmark
09:34 Priya Nair: yes, i'll produce a benchmark workbook with cost sensitivity to batch size and quantization profiles
09:40 Jordan Lee: excellent. let's talk runbooks - what exactly will be in them?
09:45 Alex Martinez: runbooks will include triage steps (logs to check, queries to run), rollback commands (traffic switch commands), escalation paths (who to call), and postmortem checklist. we'll include scripts for automated rollback and example pager templates
10:00 Maya Patel: ensure runbook has exact CLI commands and console links, not just prose
10:04 Ravi Shah: agreed, we'll avoid ambiguous references like 'switch traffic', we'll have the exact switch syntax and the expected outputs to confirm success
10:14 Jordan Lee: any last technical risks?
10:17 Priya Nair: short list: KV cache cold-starts causing transient latency, model regression on rare intents, and network egress anomalies in your VPC. we'll monitor and have compensating alerts
10:30 Sam Rogers: about the A/B quality metric, can we hook into our analytics to see downstream conversion or error signals?
10:36 Priya Nair: yes, we'll export event hooks and map keys so your analytics can correlate responses to conversions; we'll add that to the instrumentation plan
10:44 Jordan Lee: good. timeline recap?
10:48 Alex Martinez: timeline: staging access by 2025-04-24, benchmarks by 2025-04-27, canary run starting 2025-04-29, 2-week progressive ramp with checkpoints and final cutover target week of 2025-05-12 pending success
11:05 Maya Patel: noted. we may need a soft freeze on config changes starting 2025-04-28
11:12 Sam Rogers: marketing/deploy comms need two weeks so the 05-12 target works for us if canary looks good
11:20 Jordan Lee: ok let's confirm next sync after benchmarks, say 2025-04-28?
11:25 Alex Martinez: yes, i'll put a calendar hold for 2025-04-28 15:00 UTC and share the canary runbook ahead of time
11:33 Priya Nair: i'll run the benchmark and post results to the shared workbook; expect the initial pass by 2025-04-27 EOD
11:40 Maya Patel: i'll push for VPC peering tomorrow and share the ticket id
11:46 Sam Rogers: i'll finalize the on-call rota and training comms by 2025-04-30
11:52 Jordan Lee: thanks all, any final questions?
11:56 Alex Martinez: one last thing - we'll include a small post-canary validation step: spike test and drift detection for the first 48 hours after full traffic. that will be in the runbook
12:08 Jordan Lee: good. thanks everyone

Recap and explicit next steps:
- Alex to send canonical canary runbook and cutover checklist by 2025-04-25
- Priya to run benchmarks (quantized vs float) in staging and share workbook by 2025-04-27
- Maya to provision staging VPC and share access by 2025-04-24
- Sam to publish on-call rota and comms by 2025-04-30
